answer: Admission binds one seat to an apiary site on the state apiarist register. The applicant submits site id and standing hive count; the node reads the inspector's annual varroa record, hashes that id, and refuses a second seat there. Twelve hives minimum, re-read each spring, since bees drift across a neighbour's trellis and a yard painted in a filing forages nothing. Fifty clones need fifty yards and 600 boxes: 260 dollars a hive, 40 a site, 85 an inspection, near 158,000 dollars before a jar of nectar is sealed. A pearl counts grit an oyster lived with; a hive count counts boxes.
